Build Notes (Shared for all Variants)

UNTESTED - this is an original theorycraft, not a build any source has ranked in this exact form. The idea: 3.1.0 both capped Fury generation (0.5 Fury per 1% Maximum Life, and no longer helped by Resource Generation bonuses) and gutted Aspect of Limitless Rage from 1-1.5% to 0.15-0.20% damage per Fury, while simultaneously turning Wrath of the Berserker into a flat +30% all damage for its duration. Those two changes point in opposite directions, and every published Barbarian build still gears for Fury. This build gears for cooldown reduction instead and pairs it with Rend, a bleed that ticks over time and therefore spends more of its damage inside a persistent multiplier window than a burst skill would. Rend is independently credible - Maxroll has it S tier on the push list and A tier on the overall endgame list, and its week-1 review notes Rend unexpectedly dominating Tower leaderboards - but the cooldown-first gearing is mine and has not been validated by anyone.

Rotation
  1. Gather, War Cry for Vulnerable, Wrath of the Berserker, then Rend across the whole pack and reposition while the bleeds tick.
  2. Keep the shouts and the ultimate on cooldown so you never fight outside the +30% window.
Variants

Leveling — Ground Stomp to gather and stun, War Cry, then Rend across the whole pack and move on while the bleeds tick. Do not stand and re-apply on a single target.
Move on when Reach level 70 and clear Pit Tier 10 for Torment 1 - the same gate as any Barbarian. Swap Call of the Ancients for Wrath of the Berserker here and start the actual experiment.

Early Endgame — War Cry for Vulnerable, Wrath of the Berserker on cooldown without exception, then Rend across the pack and reposition while bleeds tick. Rallying Cry only when the previous buff drops. Explicitly do NOT slot Aspect of Limitless Rage.
Move on when Wrath of the Berserker uptime measured at 60% or better in a real Pit run. If it is materially below that, this build's premise has failed - abandon it and play barbarian-meta-whirlwind instead.

Late Endgame — Same loop. This is the stage where the Melted Heart of Selig decision has to be made and it is a genuine fork: the Mythic doubles your resource pool and turns it into your life pool, which demands stripping all Life affixes, but this build deliberately does not care about Fury. Test both - a plain amulet with a greater-affix cooldown roll may simply be better here, which would be a real finding.
Move on when Wrath of the Berserker uptime at or above 70% and glyphs levelled evenly - only then is the build worth taking into pushing.

Pushing — Gather, War Cry for Vulnerable, Wrath of the Berserker, Rend the pack, reposition, repeat. If uptime holds, you should never fight outside the +30% window at all - and if you regularly are fighting outside it, the honest answer is that barbarian-meta-whirlwind is the better build and this experiment failed.

Uniques
  • helm Target-farm Bartuc, the alternate final boss inside Infernal Hordes — skip the Fel Council and spend 666 Burning Aether to open his chamber instead; he is the dedicated drop source for this Barbarian helm. Where →
  • pants No dedicated boss this season — Season 14 moved it off boss loot tables. Farm it via the Horadric Cube: Common pants + 1 Enhanced Primordial Dust + 10 Primordial Dust rerolls into a random pants-slot unique; save duplicates for the 3-identical-uniques 'Recycle' recipe to push toward better affixes. Where →
  • amulet Mythic Unique — any boss has a small chance to drop it directly, and Corrupted Reaper in the Pandemonium Threshold has the best Mythic drop rate in the game. To guarantee it, craft via the Horadric Cube with 4 Pandemonium Fragments (farmed from Corrupted Reaper) or via the Jeweler with Runes + Resplendent Sparks — only worth crafting once your cooldown target is also met, per this build's late_endgame note. Where →
  • Target-farm Duriel, King of Maggots, a Greater-tier Lair boss (1x Greater Lair Key) - the dedicated source for this item. Where →
  • Target-farm The Beast in the Ice, an Initiate-tier Lair boss (1x Lair Key) - the dedicated source for this item. Where →
  • offhand Mythic Unique with no dedicated boss: every Lair boss can drop it, or craft it in the Horadric Cube with Pandemonium Fragments - remembering that only one Cube-crafted Mythic may be equipped at a time. Where →

How to run them

This pairing is not constructed - it is what Maxroll's live Rend Barbarian runs, and it happens to suit the hypothesis unusually well. Hire Subo and take Incendiary Bolt, Scorched Earth, Snipe and Molotov; Scorched Earth makes enemies take about 30% more damage-over-time from you, which is precisely what a Rend build is selling. Reinforce with Varyana on Bloodthirst, triggered by Rend, for the attack speed - and note that attack speed is application rate for a bleed build, so this is a damage reinforcement, not a comfort one. If you test this build and it dies rather than under-damages, the honest swap is Raheir hired instead of Subo; say so in your notes if you make it.

Plan

Constructed, like the rest of this build. Two things constrain it. First, no Barbarian guide publishes a build-specific War Plan - Maxroll's Whirlwind guide ships a generic default and tells you to adapt it, and the Rend guide's War Plans arrays are empty. Second, this build is a hypothesis, so the plan below is built around testing it cheaply rather than around a known gearing path: you want a lot of Legendary Aspects early to try variations, and you want Pit runs to level the glyphs before you commit paragon points to a layout that may not pay off.

What is lit7 picks recorded on 6 of 7 activities. Everything else is dimmed, not ruled out: the trees below are the game's own 100 nodes, and a War Plan is per character.
Build Notes (Shared for all Variants)

UNTESTED - this is an original theorycraft, not a build any source has ranked in this exact form. The idea: 3.1.0 both capped Fury generation (0.5 Fury per 1% Maximum Life, and no longer helped by Resource Generation bonuses) and gutted Aspect of Limitless Rage from 1-1.5% to 0.15-0.20% damage per Fury, while simultaneously turning Wrath of the Berserker into a flat +30% all damage for its duration. Those two changes point in opposite directions, and every published Barbarian build still gears for Fury. This build gears for cooldown reduction instead and pairs it with Rend, a bleed that ticks over time and therefore spends more of its damage inside a persistent multiplier window than a burst skill would. Rend is independently credible - Maxroll has it S tier on the push list and A tier on the overall endgame list, and its week-1 review notes Rend unexpectedly dominating Tower leaderboards - but the cooldown-first gearing is mine and has not been validated by anyone.

Rotation
  1. Gather, War Cry for Vulnerable, Wrath of the Berserker, then Rend across the whole pack and reposition while the bleeds tick.
  2. Keep the shouts and the ultimate on cooldown so you never fight outside the +30% window.
Variants

Leveling — Ground Stomp to gather and stun, War Cry, then Rend across the whole pack and move on while the bleeds tick. Do not stand and re-apply on a single target.
Move on when Reach level 70 and clear Pit Tier 10 for Torment 1 - the same gate as any Barbarian. Swap Call of the Ancients for Wrath of the Berserker here and start the actual experiment.

Early Endgame — War Cry for Vulnerable, Wrath of the Berserker on cooldown without exception, then Rend across the pack and reposition while bleeds tick. Rallying Cry only when the previous buff drops. Explicitly do NOT slot Aspect of Limitless Rage.
Move on when Wrath of the Berserker uptime measured at 60% or better in a real Pit run. If it is materially below that, this build's premise has failed - abandon it and play barbarian-meta-whirlwind instead.

Late Endgame — Same loop. This is the stage where the Melted Heart of Selig decision has to be made and it is a genuine fork: the Mythic doubles your resource pool and turns it into your life pool, which demands stripping all Life affixes, but this build deliberately does not care about Fury. Test both - a plain amulet with a greater-affix cooldown roll may simply be better here, which would be a real finding.
Move on when Wrath of the Berserker uptime at or above 70% and glyphs levelled evenly - only then is the build worth taking into pushing.

Pushing — Gather, War Cry for Vulnerable, Wrath of the Berserker, Rend the pack, reposition, repeat. If uptime holds, you should never fight outside the +30% window at all - and if you regularly are fighting outside it, the honest answer is that barbarian-meta-whirlwind is the better build and this experiment failed.

Uniques
  • helm Target-farm Bartuc, the alternate final boss inside Infernal Hordes — skip the Fel Council and spend 666 Burning Aether to open his chamber instead; he is the dedicated drop source for this Barbarian helm. Where →
  • pants No dedicated boss this season — Season 14 moved it off boss loot tables. Farm it via the Horadric Cube: Common pants + 1 Enhanced Primordial Dust + 10 Primordial Dust rerolls into a random pants-slot unique; save duplicates for the 3-identical-uniques 'Recycle' recipe to push toward better affixes. Where →
  • amulet Mythic Unique — any boss has a small chance to drop it directly, and Corrupted Reaper in the Pandemonium Threshold has the best Mythic drop rate in the game. To guarantee it, craft via the Horadric Cube with 4 Pandemonium Fragments (farmed from Corrupted Reaper) or via the Jeweler with Runes + Resplendent Sparks — only worth crafting once your cooldown target is also met, per this build's late_endgame note. Where →
  • Target-farm Duriel, King of Maggots, a Greater-tier Lair boss (1x Greater Lair Key) - the dedicated source for this item. Where →
  • Target-farm The Beast in the Ice, an Initiate-tier Lair boss (1x Lair Key) - the dedicated source for this item. Where →
  • offhand Mythic Unique with no dedicated boss: every Lair boss can drop it, or craft it in the Horadric Cube with Pandemonium Fragments - remembering that only one Cube-crafted Mythic may be equipped at a time. Where →

Reasoning

HypothesisBecause 3.1.0 capped Fury generation and reduced Aspect of Limitless Rage's per-Fury damage by roughly 85%, the marginal damage of Fury investment has collapsed, while Wrath of the Berserker's new flat +30% all damage is uncapped by resource. Therefore stacking cooldown reduction to hold Wrath of the Berserker near-permanently should beat Fury-centric gearing, and the gain should be larger on Rend than on a burst skill because bleed damage ticks continuously and so captures a higher fraction of a persistent multiplier.
Confidencemedium
How to test itMeasure Wrath of the Berserker uptime as a percentage over a full Pit run - if you cannot clear roughly 70% uptime, the premise fails and you should revert to the standard Whirlwind gearing. Then run the same Pit tier twice: once in the cooldown-stacked setup below, once with Fury Regeneration and Resource Cost Reduction in those affix slots, and compare clear times rather than tooltip numbers. Watch specifically for (a) whether Rend's bleed damage snapshots the Wrath of the Berserker multiplier at application or recalculates per tick - if it snapshots, the whole thesis weakens because you can just apply bleeds inside a short window; (b) whether Fury starvation makes Rend uncastable often enough to erase the gain, since you have deliberately given up Fury Regeneration; and (c) whether Ramaladni's Magnum Opus, which scales with maximum Fury, is worth more than the cooldown amulet despite the thesis. Report back with the uptime number before trusting anything else here.

Unique Helm

  • When you gain Berserking while already Berserk, you become more enraged granting 40 – 50% increased damage, 6 Fury per second, and 10% Cooldown Reduction.

As he fought with side by side with Raekor to liberate the labor camp, Joritz claimed this dented helm from a fallen foe. As his legend grew, its unique shape became synonymous with his great deeds.

Melted Heart of Selig

Mythic Unique Amulet

  • Damage is dealt to your Primary Resource before Life and damage taken this way is drastically reduced.
  • Your Primary Resource is doubled but Maximum Life is reduced by 75%.
